title: $1278 for a frame THIS GOOD! The Yoeleo G21 Altera

takeaways.text: Third-generation changes noted by the retailer-presenter: in-frame storage, a round 27.2 mm seatpost replacing the aero post, full UDH, inboard-bearing T47 and revised geometry; he still had slight toe overlap on the smallest (45) size with very large tires.
Repeats Yoeleo's T800 lay-up and claimed weights of 1,170 g ±50 g for a size-56 frame and about 480 g for the fork; the frame was not weighed.

Schwalbe Thunder Burt mountain-bike tires the presenter believed were 2.1 in fitted the size 45. Yoeleo's 42T chainring limit is realistic with a standard spindle; a 38T ring with 3 mm offset left about half a finger of gap to the stay.
The headset is close to, but not exactly, FSA ACR dimensions: a CRW bar on the stock spacer left an uneven gap, which the stock Yoeleo bar or cover avoids.
In September 2025 the frameset listed at US$1,420, or US$1,278 with the presenter's shop's 10% discount; the presenter's store sells Yoeleo.
The size-45 build with L-Twoo wireless 1×, F-Sports 40 mm wheels, large MTB tires, pedals, cages, mount and some mud weighed 8.1 kg.

Rides smoothly and feels fast on tarmac with 36 cm bars; more comfortable than the previous generation but less so than the VoiceVelo G Major. Likes: price, clearance, geometry; dislikes: weight, two stock colours, top storage hard to use while riding.

disclosure: China Cycling's founder also leads Panda Podium, a retailer of Chinese cycling products.
summary: Detailed platform walkaround, complete build, and ride context for the Altera G21; the shown components may differ from this site's estimated build.
